name: Business - Vocational Education and Training: State Funding - Against demand driven VET funding
question: The majority voted against a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org/senate/?id=2012-10-09.89.1) introduced by Greens Senator [Lee Rhiannon](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Lee_Rhiannon&mpc=Senate&house=senate), which means that it was rejected. The motion was: _That the Senate-_ _(a) notes that:_ _(i) on 20 September 2012 thousands of students, parents, teachers, staff and friends of [Technical and Further Education](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_and_Further_Education) (TAFE) rallied in Victoria, and in other states, to support TAFE students and staff who are bearing the brunt of state government budget cuts such as the [Baillieu](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Baillieu) Government’s devastating $300 million TAFE cuts, which will lead to campus closures, job losses, more course cuts, further increases to students’ fees and charges, and will damage the economy,_(Read more about the protests on ABC News [here](http://www.abc.net.au/local/audio/2012/09/20/3594595.htm). ) _(ii) the Baillieu Government’s $300 million [vocational education and training](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocational_education_and_training#Australia) (VET) budget cuts result from a drastic shift in VET market share, where private VET courses have overtaken TAFE courses for the first time, coupled with a 310 per cent growth in enrolments in private [Registered Training Organisations](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Registered_Training_Organisations) (RTOs), a failure of state and federal VET policy that TAFE should not be punished for,_ _(iii) the New South Wales Government in the week beginning 9 September 2012 delivered a $1.7 billion education budget cut that includes 800 job losses at [TAFE NSW](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TAFE_NSW) and will result in a 9.5 per cent increase in TAFE NSW course fees, and_(Read more about these NSW cuts to the education budget on ABC News [here](http://www.abc.net.au/local/stories/2012/09/13/3589397.htm) and on ABC's Lat
